about.title: Tiburon Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Tiburon's roads carry a steady mix of commuters, cyclists, and visitors heading toward the ferry terminal, and that traffic funnels through a handful of corridors: Tiburon Boulevard, Rt 131, Paradise Drive, and Cecilia Way. Public records show these routes see the bulk of reported collisions locally, with Tuesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. standing out as a common time for crashes to occur. After a wreck, the hours and days that follow matter — insurance adjusters often reach out quickly, sometimes before you've seen a doctor or reviewed the damage to your vehicle. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm, that connects injured Tiburon residents and visitors with an independent personal injury attorney working on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover. An attorney in our network can help you understand your options, preserve evidence from the scene, and communicate with insurers on your behalf so you're not navigating the process alone.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before the Insurer

items.title: California's Filing Window Is Limited
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident lawsuit in California, and that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a road maintenance agency — may be involved. An attorney can help you figure out which deadline applies before it's too late.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Affect Your Recovery
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning you can still recover damages even if you're partly at fault for the accident, though your share of fault reduces the amount. Insurers sometimes use this rule to shift blame onto you early, so it helps to have someone reviewing the facts on your side.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Work Against You
items.desc: There's no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering in a California car accident claim, but a poorly worded recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can undercut your claim's value regardless of the law. An attorney can advise you on what to say — and what to hold off on saying — while evidence is still fresh.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Tiburon?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. If a government entity, such as one responsible for maintaining a road like Paradise Drive, may share fault, that deadline can be as short as six months. It's best to have an attorney evaluate your situation early so you don't miss a shorter window.

items.question: My crash happened on Tiburon Boulevard during the Tuesday afternoon traffic — does that matter for my claim?
items.answer: The time and location of a crash don't change your legal rights, but they can be useful when reconstructing what happened, especially if traffic camera footage, witness accounts, or nearby business surveillance exists. Public records show Tuesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. are a common time for reported collisions in Tiburon, so an attorney may look at similar reports and available evidence to help support your version of events.

items.question: Will I have to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: You're generally not required to give a recorded statement to the other party's insurer, and doing so without guidance can sometimes be used to minimize your claim. An independent attorney can communicate with the insurance company on your behalf so you're not put in a position to say something that gets misinterpreted later.
